7. GENERAL

REQUiREMENTS marks or

7.1 Blade - The surface of the blade shall have no hammer other imperfections and shall be polished.
grip

7.2 Backs - Backs shall be uniformly folded and properly closed so as to the blade along the whole length. Backs shall be polished or blued over the entire exposed surface of each back. hand grip of both open and closed types of handles 7.3 Handle -The shall be so shaped that discomfort is not caused to the hand, The handle shall be centrally slit. The thickness of the handle shall not be less than 20 mm. The handles shall be polished. throughout. The devetail saws and 200 mm tenon saws shall be provided with open or closed handles whereas other sizes of tenon saws shall be provided with closed handles. The handles shall conform to the requirements of Class 5 of IS : 620-1965*.

IS : 5123 - 1969 7.4 Teeth -- The teeth shall be evenly formed and shall have tooth angles as shown in Fig. 2. The teeth shall be alternately set on either side of the blade. Approximately two-thirds ofeach tooth measured from the points shall be set, and the method of setting shall be such that the remainder of the blade shall not be deformed. The degree of set on either side shall be equal and shall be not less than 0.25 and not more than Q5 of the thickness of blade.

FOR RIPPIN
*Regardless of variations in the Rake Angle, the Gullet Angle shall remain at 60".

7.4.1 Grade 1 tenon saws shall be cross or half cross sharpened, Grade 2 half cross or straight sharpened, Grade 3 straight sharpened and Grade 4 straight sharpened or unsharpened ( see Appendix A ). 7.4.2 Dovetail saws shall be straight sharpened ( see Appendix 8. DESIGNATION 8.1 The saws shall be designated by: a) commonly used name, b) grade, c) nominal size, and d) number of this standard.

IS : 5123 - 1969 9. MARKING 9.1 The saw shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the nominal size, The year of type, grade and the manufacturer's name or the trade-mark. manufacture shall also be marked, if required by the purchaser. 9.1.1 The saws may also be marked
with the IS1 Certification Mark.

Nora -The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification hlarks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and This system, which is devised and supervised by quality control during production. IS1 and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a liccnce for the use of the ISI Certification hfark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

10. SAMPLING 10.1 Unless otherwise agreed the sampling plan and criteria be followed. 11. TESTS 11.1 Setting Test - The teeth of all saws shall be capable of being set, without breaking, by reasonable hammer blows on a setting stake, or by a suitable, correctly adjusted saw set. Two-thirds of each tooth, measured from the point shall Fs set for this test. 11.2 Straightness Test - \Vhen checked with the aid of a straight the back and blade shall be visually straight and free Dam twist.
edge to between the supplier and the purchaser for conformity as given in Appendix B shall

11.3 Performance Test-When sharpened and jet in accordance with 7.4 each saw shall cut cleanly and freely, without binding, when tested on lvell seasoned Indian oak or other suitable hardwood, both when cutting with the grain and when cutting across the grain.
